courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces students to personal safety, occupational health and safety, and environmental practices. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.
This course introduces students to employment readiness, communication skills using electronic media, and industry business practices. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the selection, use, and maintenance of hand, measuring, and power tools, fasteners, shop equipment, and reference resources. This course also introduces students to job action preparation and diagnostic procedures. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001
This course introduces students to welding safety, identification of metals, and procedures for oxy-acetylene welding and shielded metal arc welding (SMAW) Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001
This course introduces students to the safe operation of lifting and mobile equipment. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the principles of operation, repair, and service procedures performed on hydraulic and air brake systems. This course also introduces students to service and repair procedures performed on bearings, seals, tires, wheels, and hubs. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001
This course introduces students to the principles of hydraulics and the safe service, diagnostic, and repair procedures performed on hydraulic systems and components. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the basic principles of electricity and the safe service, diagnostic, and repair procedures performed on electrical components and circuits. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the basic principles of suspension and steering and the safe service, diagnostic, and repair procedures performed on suspension systems and components. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the basic principles of trailer landing gear, accessories, trailer bodies, and refrigeration and heating systems and the safe service, diagnostic, and repair procedures performed on hydraulic systems and components. Prior to the refrigeration component of this course, students must obtain an Ozone Depleting Substances Handling Certificate from the Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Institute. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the principles of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning and the safe service, diagnostic, and repair procedures performed on heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems and components. Prior to the practical component of this course, students must obtain an Ozone Depleting Substances Handling Certificate from the Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Institute. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the basic principles of internal combustion engines and their supporting systems and the safe service, diagnostic, and repair procedures performed on engines and their supporting systems and components. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the basic principles of powertrain and the safe service, diagnostic, and repair procedures performed on powertrain systems and components. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

This course introduces students to the basic principles of structural components and accessories and the safe service, diagnostic, and repair procedures performed on structural components and accessories. Prerequisite(s): HMTF 1001

admission.raw: Note: This trade program is in high demand. Visit Trades Training BC to estimate a future start date. Scheduled intakes Multiple start dates each year. Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don't meet the requirements we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Foundations of Math and Pre-Calculus 10 (50%) or Workplace Math 10 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Continuation requirements Students who wish to attend apprentice technical training must register as an apprentice with SkilledTradesBC . Foundation program students can register in the Heavy Mechanical Trades Apprenticeship programs. Recommended for success High school graduation is recommended by SkilledTradesBC. Please refer to the SkilledTradesBC website for current apprenticeship prerequisite information. A driver's licence is not required to enter the program. However, it is strongly recommended in order to move vehicles in and out of the shops. Potential students with medical or physical disabilities should contact Accessibility Services to arrange an interview with the institute's rehabilitation specialist at 604-451-6963 (telephone interview is acceptable for out of town applicants). Trades Discovery The Trades Discovery General and Trades Discovery for Women are full-time programs designed to prepare participants to successfully enter and complete a Trades Training program. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Please note that international students are not eligible to continue to an apprenticeship training program. To learn more about international student opportunities at BCIT, visit BCIT International . Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. ( CIPC : 47.0302) Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
